verdict.rationale: The simulation shows that n=60 has a low probability of recovering a stable structure with 20 features and 3 phenotypes. The conservative scenario (higher noise, lower effect size) requires n≥100. The recommended sample size is n=100.
verdict.power_analysis_note: This is a SIMULATION-based power analysis, not a closed-form calculation. It accounts for: feature dimensionality, phenotype prevalence, measurement noise, missingness, and effect size. It does NOT account for: site effects, non-normal distributions, or nonlinear relationships. A statistician should review this before finalizing.

endpoint_rewrite.OLD_endpoint: HIT-6 ≥ 50 + ICP ≤ 20 + improved papilledema — REMOVED (too broad, captures 'who has headache' not 'who has a reproducible treatment-failure phenotype')

E_SYMPTOM.name: Symptom recurrence (broad)
E_SYMPTOM.definition: HIT-6 ≥ 50 at 12 months post-VSS, regardless of ICP/papilledema status
E_SYMPTOM.what_it_captures: Who has headache — NOT specific to treatment failure
E_SYMPTOM.use: DESCRIPTIVE ONLY — not the primary discovery endpoint

E_OBJECTIVE_IIH.name: Objective IIH recurrence
E_OBJECTIVE_IIH.definition: ICP > 20 cm H2O OR papilledema worsening (Frisén grade increase) at 12 months
E_OBJECTIVE_IIH.what_it_captures: True treatment failure — the device stopped working
E_OBJECTIVE_IIH.use: EXCLUSION — these patients have R2-C1/R2-C2, not R2-C3

E_VENOUS_FAILURE.name: Venous mechanical failure
E_VENOUS_FAILURE.definition: Imaging-confirmed in-stent or adjacent restenosis at 12 months

E_RESIDUAL_HEADACHE.name: Persistent headache with normalized physiology
E_RESIDUAL_HEADACHE.definition: HIT-6 ≥ 50 at 12 months AND ICP ≤ 20 cm H2O AND papilledema improved/resolved AND no imaging-confirmed restenosis
E_RESIDUAL_HEADACHE.what_it_captures: The SPECIFIC R2-C3 phenotype — headache despite ALL objective measures being normal
E_RESIDUAL_HEADACHE.use: PRIMARY DISCOVERY ENDPOINT — this is the residual we want to explain

E_VISUAL_FAILURE.name: Visual deterioration with normalized pressure
E_VISUAL_FAILURE.definition: New visual field defect OR OCT worsening at 12 months AND ICP ≤ 20 cm H2O AND papilledema improved
E_VISUAL_FAILURE.use: SECONDARY ENDPOINT — lower prevalence but higher harm

endpoint_rewrite.primary_endpoint: E_RESIDUAL_HEADACHE — persistent headache with normalized physiology (ICP ≤ 20, improved papilledema, no restenosis). This is the SPECIFIC residual phenotype the experiment is designed to explain.
endpoint_rewrite.why_this_is_better: The old endpoint mixed 'who has headache' (too broad) with 'who has treatment failure.' The new endpoint specifically captures the R2-C3 anomaly: headache despite ALL objective measures being normal. This is the phenotype the competing models are trying to explain.

human_free_validation.REMOVED: ≥3/5 independent panel members agree structure is interpretable — HUMAN REVIEW GATE. REMOVED.

criterion_1_bootstrap_stability.name: Bootstrap cluster stability
criterion_1_bootstrap_stability.test: Cluster appears in ≥80% of 1000 bootstrap resamples with ≥80% member overlap

criterion_2_external_holdout.name: External holdout replication
criterion_2_external_holdout.test: Structure discovered in Cohort 1 replicates in Cohort 2 (prospective holdout) with AUC within 0.05

criterion_3_calibration.name: Prediction calibration
criterion_3_calibration.test: Calibration slope between 0.8-1.2 and calibration intercept within ±0.1 on holdout (Hosmer-Lemeshow p > 0.05)

criterion_4_physiological_constraints.name: Physiological constraint satisfaction
criterion_4_physiological_constraints.test: Discovered clusters must satisfy pre-registered physiological constraints: (a) venous phenotype cluster must have mean CVP > population mean, (b) migraine phenotype cluster must have mean CGRP > population mean, (c) no cluster may have ALL signals normal (that would be Model D — artifact)

criterion_5_confounder_perturbation.name: Confounder perturbation resistance
criterion_5_confounder_perturbation.test: Cluster assignments must not change by >15% when confounders (BMI, site, stent type) are permuted

criterion_6_negative_control.name: Negative control performance
criterion_6_negative_control.test: Model must NOT predict a random outcome (negative control) above AUC 0.55 — if it does, it is overfitting

decision_value_layer.the_question: Does knowing the discovered phenotype change what treatment would be selected?
decision_value_layer.the_sequence: phenotype discovery → external validation → DECISION-VALUE TEST → intervention selection → intervention effect

decision_value_test.design: Present 50 clinical vignettes (derived from real patient data) to the analysis pipeline. For each vignette, the pipeline outputs: (a) phenotype assignment, (b) recommended intervention. Compare recommended intervention vs. STANDARD OF CARE.
decision_value_test.success_criterion: Phenotype-guided recommendation DIFFERS from standard care in ≥30% of cases AND the difference is clinically actionable (maps to a real intervention that exists)
decision_value_test.failure_criterion: If phenotype-guided recommendation = standard care in ≥70% of cases, the phenotype does NOT change clinical decisions. The discovery is scientifically interesting but NOT an invention.

intervention_map.venous_phenotype: venous intervention (repeat VSS, longer stent, CPAP for OSA if venous congestion is OSA-related)
intervention_map.migraine_phenotype: migraine treatment (CGRP antagonist, migraine prophylaxis, medication-overuse detox)
intervention_map.artifact_phenotype: reclassification — no IIH treatment escalation, refer to headache specialist

decision_value_layer.why_this_matters: A phenotype can predict outcomes AND still be useless if it doesn't change what the physician would do. The decision-value test ensures the discovery has CLINICAL UTILITY, not just statistical significance.

confounding_attacks.the_threat: Could the discovered phenotype be nothing more than a proxy for measurement center, stent type, BMI, migraine prevalence, or follow-up timing?

attacks.method: Permute site labels. If cluster assignments change >15%, the phenotype is a site artifact.
Permute stent type labels. If cluster assignments change >15%, the phenotype is a stent artifact.
attacks.pass_criterion: ≤15% assignment change under stent type permutation

attacks.method: Regress out BMI from all features. Re-run clustering on residuals. If clusters disappear, the phenotype is a BMI proxy.
attacks.pass_criterion: Clusters survive BMI regression (≥80% member overlap)

attacks.method: Restrict analysis to patients WITHOUT migraine phenotype (ICHD-3 negative). If clusters disappear, the phenotype is a migraine proxy.
Normalize all features to 12-month timepoint. If cluster assignments change >15%, the phenotype is a timing artifact.
Permute medication use labels (acetazolamide, topiramate, pain medications). If clusters change >15%, the phenotype is a medication effect.

confounding_attacks.when_to_run: BEFORE real data analysis — run on synthetic data to verify the analysis pipeline is robust to confounding. THEN run on real data and apply the same tests.

existing_data_check.the_question: Can existing retrospective/registry/public data answer the FIRST falsification question before designing an expensive prospective study?

what_exists.what_it_has: Symptomatic recurrence data, ICP measurements, papilledema grades, follow-up timing
what_exists.what_it_LACKS: CVP, sinus pressure distribution, CGRP, ICP waveform/pulsatility, migraine phenotype scores
what_exists.can_it_falsify: PARTIALLY — can test Model D (artifact: what proportion of 'recurrence' has no objective findings?) and provide prevalence estimates. Cannot test Models A, B, or C (lacks the discriminating variables).

what_exists.what_it_has: CVP measurements, anterior SSS pressure, BMI, post-VSS outcomes
what_exists.what_it_LACKS: CGRP, ICP waveform, migraine phenotype, longitudinal trajectory, headache-specific outcomes
what_exists.can_it_falsify: PARTIALLY — can test Model A (venous) partially. Cannot test Models B, C, or E.

what_exists.what_it_has: Serum CGRP levels, headache persistence data, ICP measurements
what_exists.what_it_LACKS: Venous pressures, sinus distribution, compliance, longitudinal trajectory
what_exists.can_it_falsify: PARTIALLY — can test Model B (migraine/CGRP) partially. Cannot test Models A, C, or E.

what_exists.what_it_has: Headache persistence (72.2%), objective findings, surgery requirement (17%)
what_exists.what_it_LACKS: All physiological variables (CVP, CGRP, ICP waveform, etc.)
what_exists.can_it_falsify: YES for Model D — can determine what proportion of persistent headache has NO objective findings.

what_can_be_done_NOW: Model D test: use the 178-patient study + repeat-stenting series to determine what proportion of 'recurrence' has no objective findings (ICP normal, papilledema improved, no restenosis). If >50%, Model D is strongly supported.
Model A partial test: use the 2026 CVP study to verify the association between CVP and outcomes (already done — ASSOCIATION confirmed, but not PREDICTION).
Model B partial test: use the 2024 CGRP study to verify CGRP elevation in persistent headache (already done — ASSOCIATION confirmed).
Prevalence estimation: use existing data to estimate the prevalence of E_RESIDUAL_HEADACHE to refine the sample size calculation.
what_cannot_be_done_with_existing_data: Full Model C (mixture) test — requires BOTH venous AND CGRP data in the SAME patients, which no existing dataset has
Model E (data-discovered) — requires the full 20-signal panel in the same patients
Out-of-sample prediction — no existing dataset has the full signal set + outcomes
Decision-value test — requires phenotype assignments + intervention mapping
existing_data_check.recommendation:
Run the Model D test on EXISTING data FIRST. If >50% of 'recurrence' has no objective findings, the primary problem may be endpoint misclassification, not a hidden physiological state. This is the cheapest, fastest falsification test and uses data that already exists.

If Model D is NOT supported (most recurrence HAS objective findings), then the prospective study is justified. If Model D IS supported, the experiment design must be revised to focus on endpoint validation rather than phenotype discovery.

what_was_fixed: 1. Sample size: n=60 → simulation-derived (conservative minimum, higher)
2. Endpoint: broad HIT-6 → phenotype-specific E_RESIDUAL_HEADACHE (headache despite ALL objective measures normal)
3. Human panel: REMOVED → 6 machine-testable criteria (bootstrap, holdout, calibration, constraints, confounder perturbation, negative control)
4. Decision-value layer: ADDED — phenotype must change clinical decisions to be an invention
5. Confounding attacks: 6 synthetic attacks defined (site, stent, BMI, migraine, timing, medication)
6. Existing data: Model D test can be run NOW on existing data before prospective study
verdict.the_corrected_sequence: phenotype discovery → external validation → decision-value test → intervention selection → intervention effect
verdict.immediate_next_step: Run Model D test on existing data (178-patient study + repeat-stenting series). This is the cheapest, fastest falsification. If >50% of 'recurrence' has no objective findings, the problem is endpoint misclassification, not hidden physiology.
verdict.gate_status: YELLOW — study architecture is now corrected. But the FIRST falsification test (Model D on existing data) has not been run.
verdict.mechanism_status: BLOCKED — requires: (1) Model D test on existing data, (2) if Model D fails, prospective study with corrected design, (3) discovery, (4) decision-value test, (5) intervention validation
